objective: Borough-level NYC yellow taxi travel patterns Jan vs Feb 2024; identify borough with largest absolute increase in average total fare.

data_sources: taxi_zones/taxi_zone_lookup.csv (265 zones, LocationID -> Borough; read with encoding='utf-8-sig')

quality_filters.nulls: drop rows with null trip_distance / fare_amount / total_amount / PULocationID

method.borough_definition: pickup borough (PULocationID -> Borough); rows with unmapped zone or Borough in {Unknown, N/A} excluded; 6 valid borough labels kept (Manhattan, Queens, Brooklyn, Bronx, Staten Island, EWR).

metrics.trip_count: number of filtered trips per (borough, month)
metrics.absolute_increase: avg_total_fare(Feb) - avg_total_fare(Jan), signed USD, broadcast to both month rows of the borough
metrics.is_max_increase: True for the borough with max signed absolute_increase, on both of its month rows

method.interpretation_note: Per analysis_plan.json 'largest absolute increase' is taken as the max signed change (an increase). A magnitude-only reading would flag EWR (-10.65, i.e. a decrease) — reported as sensitivity only.
method.environment_note: pyarrow/pandas/matplotlib are installed in the user site-packages; run_python's isolated interpreter (-I) hides them, so scripts were executed via subprocess python3 scripts/exec_analyze.py / scripts/exec_plot.py.

findings: Bronx has the largest absolute increase in average total fare from Jan to Feb 2024: +$0.80 (35.6322 -> 36.4347).

Other positive movers are small: Manhattan +$0.29, Queens +$0.25. Brooklyn (-$0.81), Staten Island (-$4.67) and EWR (-$10.65) declined; Staten Island (68/54 trips) and EWR (284/279 trips) are very small samples.
Total filtered trip volume rose 1.39% (5,871,132 used trips; +40,584 Feb vs Jan), driven by Manhattan (+60,398) and Brooklyn (+2,698), while Queens (-22,557), Staten Island (-14) and EWR (-5) fell.
Bronx average trip distance rose 6.5147 -> 6.7729 miles (also the largest distance increase), consistent with its fare increase.
Queens keeps the longest average trips (12.34 -> 12.23 mi) and EWR the highest average total fare (~$111 -> $100) despite ~1-1.4 mi trips.

Data quality: filters removed 37,510 rows in Jan (1.27%) and 40,725 rows in Feb (1.35%); a further 11,840 (Jan) / 10,943 (Feb) filtered trips were dropped for unmapped or Unknown/N-A pickup zones, leaving 2,915,274 / 2,955,858 trips used (5,871,132 total).

validation.cross_check_vs_analysis_plan_reference: All 12 borough-month values and the winning borough (Bronx) match analysis_plan.json expected_reference_results exactly.
validation.output2_png: two side-by-side grouped bar subplots (distance left, fare right), Jan vs Feb, dpi=150, titles/labels exactly as specified; file size ~110 KB
